mainTopic: Adding a month to the year (עיבור שנה) because of the equinox (תקופה): whether the equinox day ends or begins the season, and sorting out the opinions in the ברייתא
overview: The ברייתא records a מחלוקת about how far into תשרי the autumn equinox may fall before בית דין adds a month to the year. רבי יוסי says twenty-one days. The גמרא explains that both תנאים read the פסוק 'חג האסיף תקופת השנה'. רבי יהודה needs the whole חג in the new season, while רבי יוסי needs only part of it. The גמרא then argues that both must hold the equinox day begins the new season. Two ברייתות challenge this. One says רבי יהודה holds the equinox day ends the old season. The other gives רבי יהודה twenty days, רבי יוסי sixteen days before פסח, רבי שמעון sixteen days even before סוכות, and אחרים fourteen days, and the גמרא calls this a קשיא. The גמרא then works through that ברייתא line by line. It shows that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי differ over whether the equinox day ends or starts the season. It also explains that the 'sixteen' in רבי יוסי's סוכות clause just matches the wording of his פסח clause. Finally it asks how רבי שמעון differs from the תנא קמא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: twenty-one days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי gives his number for when the year must get an extra month because of the equinox: twenty-one days.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא about adding a month to the year because the autumn equinox comes too late. רבי יוסי says the year gets an extra month only if twenty-one days of תשרי pass before the equinox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, רבי יהודה gave a smaller number (sixteen days). רבי יוסי allows the equinox to fall later in תשרי before בית דין has to add a month, so he is more lenient about the timing.

keyTerms.meaning: Season; here, the autumn equinox that starts the season of תשרי
Adding a thirteenth month to the year

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: twenty-one days.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the year is made a leap year because of the equinox only if twenty-one days of תשרי pass before it.

steps.title: Both read the same verse differently
steps.stepSummary: Both תנאים learn from 'חג האסיף תקופת השנה'. One requires the whole חג in the new season, and the other requires only part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned from one verse: 'The Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.' One Sage holds we need the whole Festival in the new season, and the other holds we need only part of the Festival in the new season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source behind the two numbers. Both תנאים read the same פסוק, but they read it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links סוכות (חג האסיף) to the new season. רבי יהודה says all of the חג must be after the equinox, so he needs an earlier cutoff. רבי יוסי is satisfied if even part of the חג falls in the new season, so his cutoff is later.

keyTerms.meaning: The Festival of Ingathering, meaning סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question. The two numbers only make sense once we know whether the equinox day itself counts as part of the new season.

phrases.english: And both of them expounded one verse:
"The Festival of Ingathering, at the turn of the year."
One Sage holds: we need the whole Festival
to be in the new season,
and the other Sage holds: we need part of the Festival
to be in the new season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning behind the two numbers in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires the whole חג in the new season, while רבי יוסי requires only part of it.

steps.title: What do they assume about the equinox day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what both תנאים hold about the day of the equinox itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up its next move. Does the day of the equinox belong to the old season or to the new one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their numbers depend on this point. If the equinox day counts as the old season, the new season starts one day later, and that changes which days of the חג are in the new season.

phrases.english: What do they hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what assumption lies underneath the two opinions just explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תנאים hold that the equinox day ends the old season or begins the new one.

steps.title: They cannot hold the equinox day ends the old season
steps.stepSummary: If the equinox day belonged to the old season, neither number would work for either opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they held that the equinox day ends the old season, then even at these numbers it would not work. The one who requires the whole Festival would not have it, and the one who requires part of the Festival would not have it either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the equinox day ends the old season, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the equinox day counts as the old season, the new season only begins the next day. Then at רבי יהודה's number the start of the חג would still be in the old season. At רבי יוסי's number the new season would begin only after the חג is already over. So neither opinion would get what its reading of the פסוק requires.

keyTerms.meaning: The equinox day ends (belongs to) the old season

phrases.english: If they hold that the equinox day concludes the old season,
then even when it is not more than this, a month would still need to be added,

phrases.aramaic: לָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כּוּלֵּיהּ חַג אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: since according to the one who says the whole Festival is needed, it is not there,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִקְצָת חַג אִיכָּא.
phrases.english: and according to the one who says part of the Festival is needed, it is not there either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possibility that the תנאים hold the equinox day ends the old season.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that view, neither תנא's number would place the חג (whole or part) in the new season.

steps.title: So both hold the equinox day begins the new season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both תנאים must hold that the equinox day starts the new season.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they hold that the equinox day begins the new season.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first option did not work, the גמרא concludes that both תנאים hold the equinox day is the first day of the new season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this assumption, both numbers work out. The disagreement is then only about the whole חג versus part of it. On this reading, the two do not disagree about the equinox day at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The equinox day begins the new season

phrases.english: Rather, they hold that the equinox day begins the new season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only remaining answer after rejecting the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both תנאים hold the equinox day begins the new season.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows they disagree about the equinox day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי יהודה holds the equinox day ends the old season and רבי יוסי holds it begins the new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'The equinox day ends the old season. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: The equinox day begins the new season.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges what it just concluded by quoting a ברייתא. That ברייתא shows רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי really do argue about the equinox day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said both agree that the equinox day begins the new season. This ברייתא says only רבי יוסי holds that. רבי יהודה holds the day ends the old season, so the assumption in step 5 is contradicted.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two phrases. גומר means the equinox day is the LAST day of the old season, and מתחיל means it is the FIRST day of the new season.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם תְּקוּפָה גּוֹמֵר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: The equinox day concludes the old season; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: יוֹם תְּקוּפָה מַתְחִיל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the equinox day begins the new season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5's conclusion that both agree the equinox day begins the new season.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that both תנאים hold יום תקופה מתחיל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא says רבי יהודה holds יום תקופה גומר, so they do not agree.

steps.title: A second ברייתא gives רבי יהודה a different number
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says the תנא קמא requires most of the month (sixteen days), while רבי יהודה requires two-thirds (twenty days).
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, it was taught: We add a month to the year only if the season is missing most of a month. How much is most of a month? Sixteen days. רבי יהודה says: two parts of the month. How much is two parts of the month? Twenty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge from another ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה's number is twenty days, not the number assumed in the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives רבי יהודה a different cutoff from the one discussed earlier. Twenty days fits his view that the equinox day ends the old season: the equinox would be on the twenty-first, and the new season would start only after the חג is over. So this ברייתא also suggests that the explanation built in steps 2–5 does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, it was taught (in a ברייתא)
We add a month to the year
Two parts out of three, meaning two-thirds

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא first explained the מחלוקת as whole חג versus part of the חג, with both agreeing that the equinox day begins the new season. Two ברייתות now challenge that. One says רבי יהודה holds the equinox day ends the old season, and the other gives him a number of twenty days.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught:
We do not add a month to the year

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה תְּקוּפָה חֲסֵירָה
phrases.english: unless the season was lacking its completion
for most of the month.

phrases.aramaic: וְכַמָּה רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ? שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם.
phrases.english: And how much is most of the month? Sixteen days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת בַּחוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: two parts of the month.
phrases.notes: Literally 'two hands'; it means two out of three parts, which is two-thirds.

phrases.aramaic: וְכַמָּה שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת בַּחֹדֶשׁ? עֶשְׂרִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: And how much is two parts of the month? Twenty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection alongside step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יהודה's number comes from requiring the whole חג in the new season, with the equinox day beginning that season.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא gives רבי יהודה twenty days. That number fits the view that the equinox day ends the old season, not the earlier explanation.

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא's opinions, and the contradiction is declared
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי (16 days before פסח, yes; before סוכות, no), רבי שמעון (also 16 days before סוכות) and אחרים (only 14 days). The גמרא declares that the sources contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: we calculate. If the old season runs sixteen days before פסח, we add a month. If it runs sixteen days before סוכות, we do not. רבי שמעון says: even sixteen days before סוכות, we add a month. אחרים say: even a small part of the month is enough. How much is a small part? Fourteen days. This is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step and then says 'קשיא!': all these different numbers do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא now gives a different amount of the month that the old season can spill into before we add a month: 20 days, 16 days, 14 days. Some also treat פסח differently from סוכות. Laid next to the earlier ברייתות, these numbers clash, and the גמרא will now start sorting them out.

keyTerms.meaning: we add a month to the year
'Others', a תנא quoted without his name
a small part (less than half) of the month

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sixteen before פסח' does not mean sixteen days before the holiday. It means the old (winter) season still runs until the 16th of ניסן, which is around the time of פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: we calculate
phrases.notes: He means we work out the date when the new season (the equinox) begins.

phrases.english: if it is sixteen days before Pesach, we add a month;

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַחַג, אֵין מְעַבְּרִין.
phrases.english: if it is sixteen days before the Festival, we do not add a month.
phrases.notes: 'The Festival' here means סוכות, in the month of תשרי.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַחַג מְעַבְּרִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: even sixteen days before the Festival, we add a month.
Others say: even a small part of the month,
and how much is a small part? Fourteen days.
This is a difficulty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא begun in step 7 and states the contradiction outright.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the different ברייתות fit together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sources give clashing amounts of days and clashing rules for פסח and סוכות, so they cannot all be right as they stand.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יוסי saying the same thing as רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא puts רבי יהודה's 20 days in תשרי next to רבי יוסי's 16 days in ניסן and asks whether they are really the same opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה says two parts of the month, which is twenty days. רבי יוסי says: we calculate, and if it is sixteen days before פסח, we add a month. But that is just רבי יהודה's view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies the ברייתא line by line. It challenges רבי יוסי: his rule seems to be exactly the same as רבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the calendar, a year in which the winter season runs 16 days into ניסן is also a year in which the summer season runs about 20 days into תשרי. So 16 days in ניסן and 20 days in תשרי describe the same years. Then why are these two separate opinions?

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת בַּחוֹדֶשׁ, עֶשְׂרִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: two parts of the month, which is twenty days.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the summer season running twenty days into תשרי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: we calculate

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח, מְעַבְּרִין.
phrases.english: if it is sixteen days before Pesach, we add a month.
That is the same as Rabbi Yehuda!
phrases.notes: The same calendar year that gives 16 days in ניסן also gives 20 days in תשרי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts studying the ברייתא's lines one at a time, beginning with how רבי יוסי compares to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה really disagree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their numbers describe the same calendar years, so the two opinions seem to be identical.

steps.title: They argue about whether the equinox day ends or starts the season
steps.stepSummary: The difference between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי is whether the day of the תקופה finishes the old season or begins the new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether the day of the equinox ends the old season or starts the new one: that is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two תנאים are not saying the same thing, because they argue about which season the equinox day belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the equinox day ends the old season, so in this kind of year he adds a month so that part of סוכות falls in the season of תשרי. רבי יוסי holds that the equinox day starts the new season, so he has no worry about סוכות, and he adds a month only so that פסח falls in the spring season. This is the same split we saw in the ברייתא of step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: the day of the equinox (when the season changes)
this is the difference between them

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same calendar numbers can lead to different rulings depending on which season the single equinox day is counted in.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם תְּקוּפָה גּוֹמֵר, וְיוֹם תְּקוּפָה מַתְחִיל –
phrases.english: Whether the equinox day ends the season, or the equinox day starts the season –
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה holds it ends the old season; רבי יוסי holds it starts the new one, as in the ברייתא of step 6.

phrases.english: that is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם תְּקוּפָה גּוֹמֵר, וְיוֹם תְּקוּפָה מַתְחִיל – אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a practical difference between the two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because their numbers describe the same years, רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה seemed to hold the same view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over whether the equinox day belongs to the old season or the new one, and that changes whether סוכות also calls for adding a month.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי's wording mean we add a month for 17 or 18 days before סוכות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's statement that 16 days before סוכות is not enough. It then draws an implication: perhaps 17 or 18 days would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: sixteen days before the Festival, we do not add a month. But according to רבי יוסי, is it only sixteen days before the Festival that we do not add a month? Does that mean that for seventeen or eighteen days we do add a month?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of רבי יוסי's words and starts a new challenge. Here it only states what his wording seems to imply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'sixteen before סוכות, we do not', רבי יוסי seems to suggest that a slightly larger number, like 17 or 18, would lead us to add a month. That would mean he does have a rule about סוכות after all. The גמרא raises this odd implication so it can press on it.

keyTerms.meaning: but then / rather, used here to open a challenge

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַחַג אֵין מְעַבְּרִין.
phrases.english: The Master said: sixteen days before the Festival, we do not add a month.
But according to Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַחַג הוּא דְּלָא,
phrases.english: is it only sixteen before the Festival that we do not,
which would mean that for seventeen and eighteen we do add a month?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַחַג הוּא דְּלָא, הָא שִׁיבְסַר וְתַמְנֵיסַר מְעַבְּרִין?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה differ, the גמרא moves on to the next part of רבי יוסי's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's statement that 16 days before סוכות is not a reason to add a month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His exact wording seems to imply that a bit more than 16 days before סוכות would be a reason to add a month. That points to a סוכות rule he never stated outright.

steps.title: The first half of רבי יוסי's statement clashes with the inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its challenge from step 11. רבי יוסי's first clause, 'sixteen days before פסח, yes,' implies that anything less is not enough. That clashes with the inference that seventeen or eighteen days before סוכות would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רבי יוסי himself say: sixteen days before פסח, yes, we intercalate, but less than that, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the inference it drew in step 11 contradicts the first half of רבי יוסי's own statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first clause we learn that a shortfall of less than sixteen days before פסח is never enough to add a month. Yet in that very same kind of year, the season before סוכות could be short seventeen or eighteen days, and the inference from the second clause would say to add a month. So the two halves of רבי יוסי's statement seem to point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't he say. This introduces a contradiction from the same speaker's own words.

phrases.english: But doesn't he say:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוסי, whose words were just used to draw that conclusion.

phrases.english: Sixteen days before פסח, yes, we intercalate;
less than that, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר: שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח – אִין, בְּצִיר – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 11 set up by setting the inference against the first clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from רבי יוסי's second clause, that seventeen or eighteen days before סוכות would be enough to add a month.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause, read precisely, says less than sixteen days before פסח is not enough, even in a year where the season before סוכות is short more days. The two precise readings of the same statement contradict each other.

steps.title: Neither case leads to intercalation; the number was just repeated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. In both cases the court does not add a month. רבי יוסי said 'sixteen' before סוכות only because he had said 'sixteen' before פסח, so the number there is not exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. In both this case and that case we do not intercalate. Since the first part taught 'sixteen days before פסח,' it also taught 'sixteen days before the Festival.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the number sixteen in the סוכות clause should not be read precisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference that seventeen or eighteen days before סוכות would work came from reading 'sixteen' as an exact limit. The גמרא says it is not a limit: according to רבי יוסי, we do not add a month for sixteen days before סוכות, and not for seventeen or eighteen either. The word 'sixteen' was used only to match the wording of the first clause.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both cases
We do not intercalate, meaning we do not add a month to the year
Since it taught in the first clause. Wording in the second clause was chosen to match the first clause, so it should not be read precisely.

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, רבי יוסי's rule for adding a month depends on the season before פסח (sixteen days). Sixteen, seventeen or eighteen days before סוכות do not cause an extra month, and the 'sixteen' in the סוכות clause is just matching wording.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'sixteen before the Festival' as an exact cutoff that would make seventeen or eighteen days enough. The number only echoes the פסח clause.

phrases.english: No, in both this case and that case we do not intercalate,
phrases.notes: 'Both' means sixteen days before סוכות, and also seventeen or eighteen days before סוכות.

phrases.english: and since it taught in the first clause
'sixteen days before פסח,'
it also taught 'sixteen days before the Festival.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי אֵין מְעַבְּרִין, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the inference: the number in the second clause was written only to match the first clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sixteen before סוכות, no' implies that seventeen or eighteen days would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי, neither sixteen nor seventeen or eighteen days before סוכות causes intercalation. The word 'sixteen' just matches the wording of the פסח clause.

steps.title: Isn't רבי שמעון the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the ברייתא: even sixteen days before סוכות is enough to add a month. It asks how this differs from the תנא קמא, who also required sixteen days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: even sixteen days before the Festival, we intercalate. Isn't that the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next opinion in the ברייתא, רבי שמעון's, and asks what he adds beyond the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the תנא קמא required 'most of the month,' which is sixteen days. רבי שמעון also says sixteen days, and his word 'even' makes it sound like he is adding a new ruling. If the number is the same, the גמרא wants to know what the actual disagreement is.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, which signals that the speaker is adding something new
The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִפְנֵי הַחַג מְעַבְּרִין.
phrases.english: Even if it is sixteen days before the Festival, we intercalate.
Isn't that the same as the first tanna?
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא said 'most of the month,' which step 7 explained as sixteen days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with רבי יוסי, the גמרא moves to the next opinion in the ברייתא, רבי שמעון's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's statement that sixteen days before סוכות is enough to add a month.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא קמא already requires sixteen days, so רבי שמעון's opinion seems to say nothing new, even though his word 'even' suggests that it does.
